lines: One view of the school, with the evidence behind every finding.
Findings from attendance, results, fees and staff records come from fixed rules, and each one shows its working.
A person decides what happens next, and the outcome is recorded.

problem.label: An illustration, not your school
beats: The principal asks how the term is going, and gets three different answers.
Attendance is in one report, results in another, fees in a ledger.
Each person answers from memory, and nobody can say why a class is slipping.
By the time the pieces are joined, the moment to act has passed.
problem.turn: Scholar Insight puts the findings in one view, with the evidence shown.

intelligence.lead: Fixed rules read the school's records and raise findings. Each one answers a plain question, and shows how it got there.

modules.asks: Where does attention need to go first?
Why was this flagged, and what is the evidence?
Which department, staff or class does this touch?
What was decided, and what happened afterwards?

intelligence.close: Rules find and explain. People decide.

ai.lead: No AI writes these findings. Fixed rules do, and a person decides what to do with each one.

owner_to_confirm: Evidence pass of 27 Nov 2026 (read-only agent) CORRECTED the checked sheet: there is NO AI or model call anywhere in the Insight / Brain code (app/Brain, the Brain controllers, config/brain.php, the Insight pages). The sheet family evidence list over-attributes: the DecisionGate, RecommendationDrafter and GroundedClaims code belongs to a separate ai_* stack that nothing in Insight calls. "Explanations must cite verified evidence or fail the check" is true only in that other stack: it is NOT said on the slide.

Approval is narrower than the sheet says. Server side: a person (the signed-in user) approves, rejects or defers a recommendation with a reason of at least 3 characters. The screen has Approve and Reject buttons only (no Defer button; Defer exists only on the Fees screen). The server does not check the current status, so a recommendation can be decided twice. The "policy requires a named person" row is a text row that nothing reads; the real safeguard is that nothing executes at all (automations are suggest-only). The slide claims only what is enforced.

Confidence: a recommendation's confidence is computed from evidence (Reasoner.php); a finding card's confidence chip is a constant typed in the rules. The slide says "recommendation", never "finding".

"Likely causes written by people and shown only where approved": the cause text lives in the rule catalogue (a PHP constant) and the screen says "cause has not been confirmed" where there is none; there is no approval record or screen for causes. The slide says "shown only where the rule library has one".

Roles: config/brain.php maps principal, admin and school admin to full access; vice principal, trustee, head of department and coordinator to manager; teacher, clerk, accountant and counsellor to analyst; students get a 403; no parent mapping was found. A test file (BrainRoleBridgeTest) expects a teacher to be read-only while the config says analyst: so whether teachers can approve is UNSETTLED and the third role lists read-only benefits. Menu rights per school live in the database (tblgroupwise_rights): not in source. Confirm the three roles and who may approve.
The "Knowledge" claim (walk department to staff and class to students) and the Analytics and KASBA claims of the sheet were not line-checked in this pass.

Not on any slide, for the owner: Decision Intelligence, Executive metrics, Memory and the process library are filled only by a demo seeder; the audit log shows a numeric actor id; owner is a role label not a person; there is no due date field; nothing sets a signal to resolved although a catalogue comment says it does.

RESEARCH TAB HIDDEN. The owner's EB list (capability framework, KASBA, O*NET and ESCO, ESO engine) is not what Insight uses: no Insight code path reads O*NET or ESCO; KASBA, capabilities and ESO are the product's own model (ESO has five or more expansions in the repos: never expand it on a slide). The same code ties those items to CCB (People and Competency). The G2G list (decision intelligence, organizational learning, human-in-the-loop) matches Insight screens but names no source. See assets/insight-research-sources.json. Decide: swap the two lists, or name external sources Insight really uses.
Pictures: stock photographs (Pexels, licence read 27 Nov 2026) and unDraw cut-outs recoloured to the deck palette; none generated.

notes.summary: Let the three lines land one at a time. Ask: who gives you the numbers about your school today, and how many different people is that?
notes.problem: Tell it as the principal asking one simple question and getting three answers. Say it is an illustration, not their school.
notes.intelligence: These are plain questions the school's own records answer. Rules raise the findings; every finding opens to its evidence and the steps. It is rules, not AI. Do not say it predicts.
notes.ai: Say plainly: there is no AI in this module. Fixed rules raise the findings. A recommendation is a draft; a person approves or rejects it with a reason; nothing runs by itself. Do NOT say a named person is required by policy, and do NOT say explanations are checked against evidence: those are not enforced here.
notes.research: Hidden for now: the research list for Insight is waiting for the owner. If it is ever shown, say what each source is, never that Scholar Insight conforms to it.
notes.features: Two groups: see the school, then decide and act. Let them point at the group their question belongs to, then open that screen.
notes.roles: Let the client name their own role first. Who may approve depends on the school's rights: say it is set per school. Every use line is an illustration.
